title: Two Islands 2.4 Miles Apart, 21 Hours Apart ⏰ #shorts
description:
In the Bering Strait, Russia's Big Diomede and America's Little Diomede are only about 2.4 miles (3.8 km) apart – but the International Date Line runs between them, so in winter Big Diomede is 21 hours ahead. That's why they are nicknamed Tomorrow Island and Yesterday Island. Little Diomede has about 80 residents (82 in the 2020 census), while the Soviet Union moved Big Diomede's people to the mainland in 1948 and today only Russian border guards live there.

Sources: Wikipedia (Diomede Islands, Diomede Alaska), Mental Floss, Geography Realm, Arctic Portal, Far Out Magazine

scenes.text: They're called the Diomede Islands, in the Bering Strait. One belongs to Russia. The other belongs to the United States.
And they are only about two point four miles apart. That's less than four kilometers.
scenes.label: APART

scenes.text: But the International Date Line runs right between them. So in winter, Big Diomede is twenty one hours ahead.
scenes.label: HOURS AHEAD

scenes.text: That's why people call them Tomorrow Island and Yesterday Island.
In nineteen forty eight, the Soviet Union closed the border and moved Big Diomede's people to the mainland.
Today, only Russian border guards live there. Little Diomede is home to about eighty people.
So from one small village in Alaska, you can wave at tomorrow every single day.
